ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $\angle B=38^\circ$, points E and F are located on sides BC and AC respectively. Fold $\triangle CEF$ along the line containing EF, so that the corresponding point $C'$ of C falls on AB, and $CE=BC$, what is the measurement of $\angle AFC'$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle A=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B+\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle C=90^\circ-38^\circ=52^\circ$,\\
$\because$ folding $\triangle CEF$ along the line containing $EF$, such that the corresponding point of $C$, denoted $C'$, falls on $AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $C'E=CE=BC'$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=\angle C'EF=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-38^\circ)=71^\circ$, $\angle CFE=\angle C'FE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CFE=\angle C'FE=180^\circ-\angle C-\angle CEF=180^\circ-52^\circ-71^\circ=57^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AFC' = 180^\circ-\angle CFE-\angle C'FE=180^\circ-57^\circ-57^\circ=\boxed{66^\circ}$.

raw_record.original_question: As shown in the figure, in $\triangle ABC$, $\angle A=90^\circ$, $\angle B=38^\circ$, points E and F are located on sides BC and AC respectively. Fold $\triangle CEF$ along the line containing EF, so that the corresponding point $C'$ of C falls on AB, and $CE=BC$, what is the measurement of $\angle AFC'$?
raw_record.answer:
\textbf{Solution:} Given $\because$ $\angle A=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle B+\angle C=90^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle C=90^\circ-38^\circ=52^\circ$,\\
$\because$ folding $\triangle CEF$ along the line containing $EF$, such that the corresponding point of $C$, denoted $C'$, falls on $AB$,\\
$\therefore$ $C'E=CE=BC'$\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CEF=\angle C'EF=\frac{1}{2}(180^\circ-38^\circ)=71^\circ$, $\angle CFE=\angle C'FE$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle CFE=\angle C'FE=180^\circ-\angle C-\angle CEF=180^\circ-52^\circ-71^\circ=57^\circ$,\\
$\therefore$ $\angle AFC' = 180^\circ-\angle CFE-\angle C'FE=180^\circ-57^\circ-57^\circ=\boxed{66^\circ}$

Point C' is drawn on AB, point E is drawn on BC, and point F is drawn on AC; EF is the crease, C'E and C'F formed after folding are solid lines, while the original CE and CF are indicated in dashed-line directions. The problem gives ∠A=90° and ∠B=38°, and asks for ∠AFC'.

From ∠A=90° and ∠B=38°, obtain ∠C=180°−90°−38°=52°. When folding along EF, the corresponding point of C is C', while E and F on the crease do not move, so EC'=EC, FC'=FC, and EF respectively bisects ∠CEC' and ∠CFC'. Point C' is drawn on AB, point E is drawn on BC, and point F is drawn on AC; EF is the crease, C'E and C'F formed after folding are solid lines, while the original CE and CF are indicated in dashed-line directions. The problem gives ∠A=90° and ∠B=38°, and asks for ∠AFC'.
Reasoning: In the figure, E is a non-endpoint on BC, so if it is literally written as CE=BC, then in the non-degenerate case it would contradict CE<BC; therefore this length condition should be understood as CE=BC' according to the condition consistent with the figure and the folding relation. From ∠A=90° and ∠B=38°, obtain ∠C=180°−90°−38°=52°. When folding along EF, the corresponding point of C is C', while E and F on the crease do not move, so EC'=EC, FC'=FC, and EF respectively bisects ∠CEC' and ∠CFC'. Also CE=BC', hence EC'=BC', so in triangle BEC', BC'=EC'. Because C' is on AB and E is on BC, ∠C'BE=∠ABC=38°, and thus the other base angle ∠BEC' of isosceles triangle BEC' is 38°. B, E, C are collinear, and EB and EC are opposite rays, therefore ∠CEC'=180°−38°=142°. EF bisects ∠CEC', so ∠CEF=∠FEC'=71°. In triangle CEF, CE lies along CB and CF lies along CA, therefore ∠ECF=∠BCA=52°, so ∠CFE=180°−52°−71°=57°. Folding symmetry gives ∠EFC'=∠CFE=57°. Also A, F, C are collinear, and FA and FC are opposite rays, so ∠AFC'=180°−∠CFE−∠EFC'=180°−57°−57°=66°.
